source.title: Local minima in training of neural networks
source.authors: G. Swirszcz; W. Czarnecki; Razvan Pascanu

page_placements.theme: Fitting effort depends on geometry, target complexity and optimization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or corruption affecting the study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives constructed examples and optimization outcomes that bear on whether training can fit the data, but it does not test random image labels using the original generalization experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports local minima and convergence rates on small constructed classification and regression datasets. Those results bear on optimization on unstructured data only insofar as explicitly tested; it does not test random relabelings, shuffled or noise inputs, generalization under label noise, regularization, or the real-versus-noisy learning order. Cited findings are not extracted as this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes bad local minima on deliberately constructed classification and regression datasets. It neither tests nor uses random-label fitting, and its optimization counterexamples do not address any of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors construct strongly suboptimal local minima and training failures, argue that convergence analyses need assumptions reflecting concrete data and architectures, and hypothesize that well-behaved learning depends on data structure.
record.recipe_differences: Constructed small datasets and analyzed local minima and convergence outcomes, rather than randomly relabeling image datasets and measuring generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: On flattened XOR, convergence varies with activation, optimizer, dataset and hidden-unit count; the paper states full-batch methods do not always succeed and that Adam does not help compared with SGD on that task.

fits_no_version.finding: The constructed sigmoid classification example has a local minimum with 40% accuracy, while another weight point achieves 80%; a further convergence point achieves 70%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small sigmoid networks can have strongly suboptimal convergence points on specially constructed classification datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-unit ReLU regression network has both a perfect-fit global solution and a suboptimal local minimum on six constructed points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational capacity for perfect fit does not exclude suboptimal local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: For two hidden units, convergence percentages differ across XOR versus flattened XOR, activation, and optimizer, including 0% for Adam with sigmoid units on flattened XOR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization success on small structured classification datasets depends on data geometry, activation, and optimizer.

record.problems: The empirical convergence table gives percentages but does not state the number of random initializations. The main local-minimum constructions use small synthetic datasets, not image datasets. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 1 values are included as separate rows by dataset and activation; the paper does not state the run count.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and slowdown with increasing label corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and progressive test degradation across random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Random initialization is not random labeling. Table 1 reports convergence success percentages, not convergence speed. Its hidden-unit counts 3–7 are omitted despite the record's assertion that no rows were omitted; these additional results also bear on none of the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random labeling experiment or test error at chance; the reported constructed datasets are not random image labels.
No comparison of time to fit true versus random labels, or convergence slowdown as corrupted-label fraction changes.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No sweep over randomly corrupted label fractions or joint training/test error measurements.
No weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or removal-of-regularization comparison.
No measurement of learning order for real patterns versus noisy or random labels.
